correctness.rationale: The regular polygon is the intersection of equally spaced halfplanes at apothem r. Nearest-normal ray distances are r sec(t). For even n opposite ray gaps coincide; for odd n they are t and b-t, proving the two distribution identities. Folding proves exact increasing quantiles. A trigonometric secant addition identity gives strictly increasing odd-to-2n rational transport with positive denominator for every n>=3. Direct secant and tangent integration proves both moment formulas. Uniform second-order Taylor expansions yield strong (coupled all-Lp) rescaled limit laws and exact 4/45 versus 1/180 variance factors. The self-contained standard-library verifier completed 1,958 finite checks including edge-by-edge ray geometry and numerical moment integrations; finite experiments are supportive rather than an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The center-constrained isotropic chord is a canonical central tomography statistic of a regular polygon, distinct from the ordinary offset-random chord. The new theorem describes the complete distributions, exact quantiles, and an unusual explicit monotone coupling between odd n and even 2n polygon chord laws. Its nondegenerate n²-scaled full limits and factor-sixteen difference in n^4-scaled variances quantify a geometrically natural parity effect in circular approximation. These are structural statements beyond evaluating a single easy chord average; their precise invariant follows naturally from radial-section sampling.
